title: Spotting and Stopping Brute-Force Attacks
intro: Any server with SSH open to the internet gets thousands of password guesses a day. Most are harmless noise against a key-only server, but you should know how to read them, spot the one that succeeded, and throttle the rest automatically.

steps.prompt: Show the most recent failed login attempts (the bad-login log), first 10 lines.
steps.explanation: Automated guesses at common usernames: admin, oracle, root, ubuntu.
steps.why: lastb reads /var/log/btmp (failed logins), and last reads /var/log/wtmp (successful ones). Usernames like 'oracle' and 'ubuntu' on a server that doesn't have them show it's a botnet dictionary attack, not a targeted one.

steps.prompt: Rank the source IPs of failed password attempts in /var/log/auth.log, top 5.
expected_commands: grep 'Failed password' /var/log/auth.log | awk '{print $(NF-3)}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5
grep "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log | awk '{print $(NF-3)}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5
steps.explanation: Two IPs account for most attempts. 198.51.100.23 is the office, probably someone mistyping.
steps.why: The grep | awk | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn pipeline is the universal 'top N' from linux-tutorial-002. $(NF-3) picks the IP by counting from the end of the line, because the start of the line varies ('invalid user X' adds words).

steps.prompt: The important question: did any attempt succeed from an IP that isn't yours? Show all accepted logins in /var/log/auth.log.
steps.fake_output: Sep 28 08:02:11 srv-web-01 sshd[2211]: Accepted publickey for deploy from 198.51.100.23 port 50412 ssh2: ED25519 SHA256:k3JqZ0
steps.explanation: Only one success: your deploy user, by key, from the office.
steps.why: Thousands of failures are noise; one unexpected 'Accepted' is an incident. 'Accepted password' from an unknown IP is the line that starts mystery-linux-006. Alert on successful logins from new sources, not on failures.

steps.prompt: Check fail2ban's SSH jail: how many IPs are banned right now.
steps.fake_output:
Status for the jail: sshd
|- Filter
|  |- Currently failed: 3
|  `- Total failed:     7215
`- Actions
   |- Currently banned: 4
   |- Total banned:     211
   `- Banned IP list:   218.92.0.112 103.45.12.9 45.227.254.8 198.51.100.23
steps.explanation: Four IPs are banned, including the office IP 198.51.100.23.
steps.why: fail2ban watches the logs and adds temporary firewall bans after N failures. It cuts noise and slows brute force, but it's not a substitute for key-only authentication, and it can ban your own people. Add the office range to 'ignoreip' in jail.local.

steps.prompt: Unban the office IP 198.51.100.23 from the sshd jail.
steps.why: A ban on a shared office or VPN exit IP blocks everyone behind it. Unban, then fix it permanently with ignoreip, because otherwise the next person to mistype a password bans the whole office again.
